heroLead: New Stanton sits right where I-70 meets the Pennsylvania Turnpike, a highway crossroads that's grown around farmland where Marcellus operators have leased and drilled for over a decade.
intro: The interchange itself gets most of the attention, warehouses and truck stops now cover ground that used to be entirely agricultural, but the mineral rights under the surrounding townships haven't changed just because commercial development moved in. If your family retained oil and gas rights when land near New Stanton was sold or developed, those rights are worth evaluating separately from what's built above them.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around New Stanton directly. We'll trace your title and check current production status before making an offer.

sections.heading: Commercial Growth Over Farmland Minerals
paragraphs: New Stanton's transformation into a logistics hub happened over the same years that Marcellus leasing was active throughout Westmoreland County, and the two developments often involve completely separate transactions on the same underlying land. A mineral reservation from a farm sale decades ago can still be valid today regardless of what's since been built on the surface.
This part of Westmoreland County sits in the wet-gas Marcellus window, with Utica potential deeper still, and operators have maintained interest in the surrounding acreage for years.

sections.heading: Tracing Title Through Commercial Development
paragraphs: We research your chain of title through the Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds in Greensburg, working through any commercial-era transactions to confirm what mineral rights your family retained, if any, when the surface changed hands.
This kind of research takes more care than a straightforward rural farm title, and we do it thoroughly before discussing terms.

sections.heading: What We'll Explain Before Any Offer
paragraphs: Once title and current production status are confirmed, we'll walk through your division order and royalty history so you understand your interest fully.

faqs.question: My family's land near New Stanton was sold for commercial development. Do we still own the minerals?
faqs.answer: Possibly, if the sale included a mineral reservation. We research your specific deed to confirm what your family retained.

faqs.question: Does commercial surface use reduce my mineral interest's value?
faqs.answer: Not directly. Mineral value depends on the formation below and production activity, not what's built on the surface above.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling connected to interests near New Stanton?
faqs.answer: We check current activity specific to your parcel's unit as part of our review, since it varies across this part of Westmoreland County.
